question_text: What are the ΔH sign conventions for exothermic and endothermic reactions?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Exothermic sign
lines: Exothermic reaction: heat is released to
The products have lower enthalpy than the
steps.why: ΔH = H(products) − H(reactants). When heat is released the products hold less enthalpy than the reactants, so the difference is negative.
common_mistakes: Writing ΔH positive for heat released — released heat means the system's enthalpy has decreased, so ΔH < 0.
steps.memory_tip: Heat out means enthalpy down, so the sign is negative.
steps.margin_note: Sign plus one line of reason.

steps.label: Endothermic sign
lines: Endothermic reaction: heat is absorbed from
The products have higher enthalpy than the
steps.why: Absorbed heat is stored as extra enthalpy in the products, so H(products) − H(reactants) comes out positive.
common_mistakes: Giving the sign with no reason — the enthalpy comparison is what shows understanding.
steps.memory_tip: Endo, energy enters: the sign is plus. Exo, energy exits: the sign is minus.
steps.margin_note: Box the two signs together as the final line.

insider_note: Write both the sign and the reason — products lower or higher in enthalpy — because the sign alone reads as a guess.
